subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default to cleanup across fresh and existing jobs, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` remain invalid and one-shot-only?
rationale: The linked bug fix and the related strict-validation PR encode opposite cron lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects existing persisted jobs, session retention, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Complete cleanup default
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require an upgrade/load/doctor path for existing omitted isolated recurring jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation direction after documenting recovery for existing recurring jobs.

options.title: Accept fresh-create only
options.body: Land the new default only for newly created jobs and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete cleanup default
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require an upgrade/load/doctor path for existing omitted isolated recurring jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on cron store/default compatibility, and steipete has recent history in that store boundary.
